themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what a tool will do next, they build one door they own and force every action through it. The reason is simple: a sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models again proposed a proxy or gateway with per-agent credentials, hard rate, budget and audience caps, a kill switch, or a read-only start, and the same instinct appears as a shared pre-send eligibility check in journey orchestration and as expiring daily cohorts in downstream consent.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Several problems have no answer key to check your work against, and the thing being measured often changes while you measure it. So the models' first move is usually to manufacture a truth set of their own.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization has no stable denominator because answers are personalized and stochastic, incrementality faces platforms that adapt to the test itself, identity resolution has no verified record of who is who, and the B2B intent answers note that validation data is a biased sample that arrives quarters late.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, an ad budget, or a buying conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, model, or private chat that now holds it. Effects and compliance can only be estimated from outside, and the parties holding the answers have little reason to open up.
themes.evidence: The consent answers say deletion inside ad platforms and trained models can only be inferred statistically, the incrementality answers say platforms conceal how treatment changes and lack incentive to expose assignment logs, the B2B answer says evaluation happens in private channels tags cannot reach, and the agent execution answers say vendor APIs never expose what an action will do.

themes.name: Politics, Not Plumbing
themes.plain: Several problems look like missing technology but are really fights over money, ownership, and whose reported number has to change. No schema, standard, or credential can settle that.
themes.evidence: The semantic layer answers call conflicting definitions of "active customer" a political settlement wearing a data modeling costume, the journey orchestration answers say no one has authority to price a customer's attention or to reward channels for staying quiet, and the agent traffic answers say no party has leverage to make everyone accept credentials.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: Some of the hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and implied claims, and no rule set captures that. The models keep concluding that human judgment can be narrowed to a smaller, safer box, not removed.
themes.evidence: The content governance answers agree that deciding whether copy makes a claim at all is the same semantic judgment the system was meant to avoid, and start by mining past legal rejections to build a locked library of approved claims, while the semantic layer answers say context-dependent meaning cannot be flattened into one global definition.
